articles.title_orig: Nebius falls 10% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook
articles.title_zh: Nebius falls 10% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook
articles.content_orig:
Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance.
Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:
It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts.
Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier.
The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing .
In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion.
Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion.
The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion.
Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion.
Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout.
The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%.
Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report.
Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing.
The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress.
Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 8 a.m. ET.

articles.title_orig: Apex Neural Rendering Challenges NVIDIA DLSS With Up To 2.4X Faster Frame Generation, 62% Lower VRAM Usage, And Broad GPU Support
articles.title_zh: Apex Neural Rendering Challenges NVIDIA DLSS With Up To 2.4X Faster Frame Generation, 62% Lower VRAM Usage, And Broad GPU Support
articles.content_orig:
NVIDIA DLSS may have a promising new competitor. Apex Compute has introduced Apex Neural Rendering (ANR), a cross-platform neural rendering suite that reportedly delivers up to 2.4X faster frame generation, superior image quality, and substantially lower GPU memory consumption than NVIDIA's technology. Better still, gamers can already try it for themselves — or at least its (Multi) Frame Generation component, which is currently available in beta .
Announced through an official X thread , ANR consists of three components: Frame Generation (FG), Super Resolution (SR), and Ray Reconstruction (RR) . Frame Generation is currently available in beta , while its upscaling and ray-reconstruction models remain in development.
One of ANR's most interesting features is its unusually broad compatibility, encompassing considerably older hardware that lacks official NVIDIA DLSS (Multi) Frame Generation support:
The beta supports Windows 10/11 alongside Linux and SteamOS through Proton . Apple silicon is also supported through a separate native Metal test kit for macOS 26 and newer.
Performance looks promising, at least according to Apex Compute's internal benchmarks . On a GeForce RTX 5090 at 3840×2160, ANR FG requires 1.01 milliseconds per generated frame in 2X mode , compared to 1.26 ms for NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. In 4X mode , the figures drop to 0.61 ms and 0.82 ms , respectively.
GPU memory consumption is another claimed advantage, with ANR requiring just 214 MB versus NVIDIA's 562 MB at 4K, representing a reduction of approximately 62% . Its neural network weights are also remarkably compact, occupying merely 0.17 MB .
Although Apex advertises up to 2.4X faster frame generation in certain tests, its published RTX 5090 measurements suggest more modest processing-time improvements. These results concern the cost of generating additional frames rather than equivalent increases in actual gaming FPS .
Image quality is another major selling point. Apex's interactive comparisons demonstrate improvements in challenging scenarios involving particles, moving objects, water, vegetation, and disocclusion artifacts .
The company has also published The Last of Us Part II Remastered and Hogwarts Legacy video showcases. Its internal CGVQM-5 , ColorVideoVDP , and PSNR quality measurements consistently favor ANR over NVIDIA DLSS FG, although independent testing is still necessary .
Interested gamers can download the latest ANR Frame Generation beta from GitHub . Installation uses OptiScaler , with separate packages for games that already have it installed and those that don't. Users extract the files, run the installer against the game's executable directory, and enable (multi) frame generation through the game's graphics settings .
The latest FG V.B14 release , published on November 12 , additionally addresses a Windows compatibility issue that prevented certain games from launching with older Visual C++ runtimes.
Apex has also released an interesting utility called nr-record , which allows users to capture frame-generation inputs and replay them through competing implementations for direct image-quality comparisons .
One important caveat is that ANR's (multi) frame generation implementation is not yet open-source , with its developers promising to release the source code later. As an experimental beta , compatibility issues and visual artifacts should also be expected .
Nevertheless, ANR represents an intriguing development for gamers seeking alternatives to proprietary (multi) frame generation implementations, particularly those running older graphics cards. As we've previously reported , unofficial efforts to bring advanced DLSS (Multi) Frame Generation capabilities to older RTX hardware have already made substantial progress.

articles.title_orig: Honda Secretly Showed Dealers Its Future Models, Including The Element. Here's What They Said
articles.title_zh: Honda Secretly Showed Dealers Its Future Models, Including The Element. Here's What They Said
articles.content_orig:
Honda has given dealers an early look at several upcoming models, and there's quite a bit to look forward to. The seventh-generation CR-V is getting a major redesign and will drop gasoline-only powertrains, while the Accord is set for a substantial facelift. There's also a new Pilot on the horizon, a tougher-looking Ridgeline, and perhaps the biggest surprise of all: the return of the quirky Element.
The previews took place during a dealer meeting in Las Vegas earlier this week. Although Honda hasn't officially released images or technical specifications, retailers who attended the event shared some juicy tidbits with Automotive News . The biggest surprise from the dealer meeting was confirmation that Honda is working on bringing back the Element.
Production of the original Element ended in 2011, but Honda apparently believes there's still room for another quirky SUV. Dealers were shown a silhouette that reportedly retains the original's boxy proportions and even the rear-hinged doors. Honda didn't provide a launch date, but insiders claim production will get underway in Q2 2029.
Next-generation Honda Element rendering by Motor1
The revived Element is expected to be an adventure-oriented hybrid crossover positioned between CR-V and HR-V. Honda is targeting younger buyers and urban adventurers, with all-wheel drive at least as an option being an educated guess. As many as 100,000 vehicles are reportedly planned for its first full year of production.
That's an ambitious target for a nameplate that has been dormant for 18 years. Still, bringing back some of the original's personality could give Honda something different in an SUV market increasingly filled with lookalike crossovers.
Next-generation Honda Ridgeline rendering by Motor1
Next-generation Honda Ridgeline rendering by Motor1
The Ridgeline, meanwhile, is getting a tougher appearance for 2028 . A rugged concept shown to dealers featured an aggressive front grille, a roof-mounted light bar, and a distinctive bed-rail system. One retailer says "the redesign is more upscale and will also appeal to entry-level luxury buyers."
The doors also featured a more pronounced lower curve, which dealers who attended the private meeting said reminded them of the Toyota Tacoma . Honda appears keen to give its unibody pickup a more adventurous personality, although it's unclear how much of the concept's styling will make it into production.
Separately, also arriving in 2028, Honda will rebadge the Mitsubishi Triton/L200 as a body-on-frame pickup tailored to certain Asian markets.
Honda Pilot XXL rendering by Motor1
Honda Pilot XXL rendering by Motor1
Honda also offered a brief glimpse of the next-generation Pilot through a video. The three-row SUV appears to be getting a more futuristic design, with triangular headlights and taillights and substantially revised bodywork.
Oddly enough, dealers didn't mention the rumored larger three-row SUV that Honda is reportedly developing as a more spacious alternative to the Pilot. The automaker has yet to confirm the model officially, so it's unclear whether it will arrive alongside the next-generation Pilot or later.
Next-generation Honda Accord rendering by Motor1
Next-generation Honda Accord rendering by Motor1
The Accord is also getting a visual makeover, although it won't be a full redesign just yet. Honda previewed a substantial midcycle refresh scheduled for the second half of 2027.
The current sedan's relatively conservative styling will give way to a more futuristic look. Dealers were shown a car featuring a sweeping hood, a premium-looking grille, and slim headlights inspired by the upcoming CR-V. One retailer described the redesign as more upscale, adding that it should appeal to entry-level luxury buyers.
Honda apparently didn't mention the rumored Crosstour revival . As previously reported, the automaker is said to be working on a lifted, hybrid-powered Accord hatchback that would effectively bring back the Crosstour nameplate. The model is reportedly planned for 2029, but dealers apparently didn't get a preview of it at the Las Vegas meeting.
Perhaps the biggest product reveal was arguably the seventh-generation CR-V . Behind closed doors, Honda allegedly showed dealers the redesigned crossover ahead of its planned showroom debut next summer. The new model will adopt a more muscular appearance, featuring pronounced rear haunches and an upright, boxy front end.
The headlights will be particularly slim, measuring approximately 1.5 inches (3.8 centimeters) in height, while the rear will feature a full-width taillight signature. The rear is said to have a cleaner look, with the wiper tucked beneath the roof spoiler; a design solution popularized by Range Rover and later adopted by Hyundai, Kia, and other automakers.
The cabin will receive a substantial upgrade, too. Higher trim levels will feature a large 15.4-inch touchscreen, while today's chunky gear selector will become a stalk behind the steering wheel, freeing up space on the center console. The updated Honda emblem will also appear on the steering wheel.
Under the hood, the next CR-V will be available exclusively with hybrid power. Honda reportedly expects the redesigned crossover to exceed 400,000 U.S. sales in its first full year after it arrives at dealers next summer. Dealers have high hopes, with one retailer saying "the CR-V’s going to be a butt-kicker” while another projects that "it’s going to sell like crazy.”

articles.title_orig: What Jensen Huang said about the next Nvidia CEO, weeks before affair scandal hit
articles.title_zh: What Jensen Huang said about the next Nvidia CEO, weeks before affair scandal hit
articles.content_orig:
Weeks before Jensen Huang's extramarital affair scandal rocked Nvidia, the CEO made comments about his succession that now seem eerily prescient.
"Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired," Huang told Bloomberg's "The Circuit" in a video released on Thursday and recorded on October 14.
Huang, who has led Nvidia for 33 years, was asked during the interview whether his daughter, Madison Huang — a senior director of product marketing for physical AI at Nvidia — was in line to take over.
"First of all, I don't hope the job on her," Huang said. "And the reason for that is because if that's their aspiration, Spencer or Madison's, they have to go earn it." Spencer is Huang's son, who works as Nvidia's director of robotics product.
Huang's newly released comments come following a week of tumult for Nvidia. The CEO admitted on Sunday to being "unfaithful" to his wife while the company's board said it was investigating whether he was targeted by a foreign-intelligence effort.
The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had a second affair with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reported directly to him, citing five unnamed former employees.
On Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to remove Huang , sending the company's shares down as much as 8% in after-hours trading. Nvidia did not immediately respond to Business Insider's request for comment.
The reports have raised a question that has long shadowed the world's most valuable chip company: Who, if anyone, is ready to replace Huang ?
Nvidia has not publicly named a successor.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Its famously flat structure, in which Huang has as many as 60 direct reports, has made it difficult to identify a clear No. 2.
Analysts and former employees have pointed to CFO Colette Kress, who could serve as an interim leader, and Ian Buck, the longtime executive who leads Nvidia's data-center and accelerated-computing business, as potential contenders.
Huang said last month that he hoped the next CEO would come from inside Nvidia — even if he said at the time he had no intention of leaving soon.
"I'm really hoping that the next CEO of the company's already at the company," he told Bloomberg . "But 20 years from now, I hope I stay healthy and I hope I continue to earn my keep."
Huang said it was his job to ensure Nvidia develops its own next CEO.
"We should create the conditions by which the company continues to thrive," Huang said, "and that the next leader of the company is already at Nvidia."
The CEO said running Nvidia carries responsibilities that should not be taken lightly. "I'm responsible for an entire industry," Huang said. "The pressure of being the CEO is high, and it's supposed to be high."

articles.title_zh: Samsung's Galaxy S27 colors just leaked, and there's an iPhone 18 Pro surprise
articles.content_orig:
If you were waiting for the upcoming Samsung Galaxy S27 lineup to drop before upgrading your smartphone, we have some bad news, particularly if you were hoping for some premium camera updates.
According to a new leak from Samsung news outlet SammyGuru , Samsung doesn't seem to have any major camera upgrades in store for the upcoming line of devices.
Another recent leak suggested that the Samsung Galaxy S27 line would see a big camera redesign. However, based on the SammyGuru report, there may not be too much new when it comes to the cameras themselves — at least for the S27 and S27 Plus models.
In fact, if you have a Samsung Galaxy S26 and are considering an upgrade to the Galaxy S27 or Galaxy S27 Plus, it looks like there will be no change to the cameras at all. Both the S27 and S27 Plus will reportedly be equipped with a 50MP main camera with a Sony IMX955 or Samsung S5KGNG sensor, SammyGuru reported. The ultrawide lens will reportedly be the same 12MP Sony IMX564, as well as the same 10MP 3x telephoto lens and 12MP selfie camera. SammyGuru reported that the S27 Ultra and S27 Pro will both get a new 200MP main camera with a Samsung S5KHP6 sensor. The S27 Ultra's predecessor, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra , has a Samsung S5KHP2 sensor, so there is a change here between the two device generations.

articles.title_orig: Boy found alive after 6 days lost in Australian wilderness: "He's grounded for life"
articles.title_zh: Boy found alive after 6 days lost in Australian wilderness: "He's grounded for life"
articles.content_orig:
A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.
The boy, whom police identified only as William, had begun camping with a teenage friend when he disappeared last Friday near Walhalla, a former gold-mining town 185 kilometers (115 miles) east of Melbourne, police said.
A police helicopter crew found him surrounded by wilderness lying asleep on a flat rock beside a creek, and he was later reunited with his mother. William was in good spirits and mostly in good health, the police statement said.
Video shot from the rescue helicopter showed he was shirtless and sunburned. He was wearing shorts and boots and was using towels as blankets.
"I'm just over the moon that he's alive," his mother, Elizabeth, told reporters. The AP has decided not to provide her family name to avoid identifying her son.
"And he's never leaving the house again. He's grounded for life. He's not going anywhere ever again," she joked.
Police video showed Elizabeth embrace her son after the rescue helicopter landed to complete its mission.
William was later taken to a hospital for his health to be monitored, police said.
"Amazingly, William is in good spirits and for the most part, in good health," they said in the statement.
William's family have said he has Level 2 autism. That requires "substantial support," according to the Australian advocacy group Autism360.
Such a person may have marked deficits in verbal and non-verbal social communication and rely heavily on routines and predictable activities. Disruption can cause significant distress.
The Southern Hemisphere spring weather had been mild for the past week in the alpine region where William was lost and there had been little rain.
Elizabeth had dropped off her son and his friend last Friday for a weekend of camping. William walked a short distance from the campsite to the drop-off location to collect more camping equipment but never returned to his friend, police said.
After becoming lost, William trekked for days up and down "some very steep terrain," Acting Police Inspector Jason Benbow said.
He spent the last two days where he was found at the creek, trapped by the steepness of his surrounds 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) from the his camp site, Benbow said.
"He woke up to the sound of the helicopter, gave them a thumbs up and they winched him to safety," Benbow told reporters.
The extensive police search for him involved more than 100 emergency services personnel and volunteers.
There have been other dramatic rescues in Australia's wilderness in recent years.
In 2025, a German tourist was found alive in Australia's remote Outback, 12 days after she went missing. She was found just a day after officials and local media said an Australian surfer , who had been feared lost at sea, was rescued after spending a night on an uninhabited island miles from where they had walked into the water.
In 2019, an Australian woman missing for three days was rescued after the SOS message she scrawled in the sand was spotted on a surveillance camera.
The successful rescues have included animals as well. Last year, a runaway dog was captured after a 529-day adventure in Australia as she roamed an island teeming with kangaroos, possums, koala bears and penguins.
Agence  France-Presse contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Spain: Housing crisis prompts first general strike in 14 years, before hundreds of thousands join protest
articles.title_zh: Spain: Housing crisis prompts first general strike in 14 years, before hundreds of thousands join protest
articles.content_orig:
Authorities in Spain say that despite pouring rain, some 120,000 citizens took to the streets of the capital, Madrid, on Wednesday evening after millions of striking workers brought Europe's fourth-largest economy to a standstill under the motto "Salaries. Housing. Prices" in the country's first general strike in 14 years earlier in the day.
The massive turnout came in response to housing shortages and unbearably high rents.
City officials in Barcelona said 55,000 people attended evening marches there as they walked behind a huge banner reading "Live. Not just survive." Housing activists in the city said the turnout was far larger, claiming that 400,000 had hit the streets.
As has been the case in other demonstrations across the Europea of late , peaceful protests later gave way to small groups of marauding young men who smashed storefront windows along Barcelona's main shopping street. They also set fire to dumpsters and shot fireworks at police when they arrived.
Earlier on Wednesday, workers across Spain gathered en masse, marching and setting up picket lines despite stormy weather in many areas of the country.
Symbolized by the eviction and death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in Madrid earlier this year, the crisis has also prompted a snap election set for November 29.
The government of left-wing Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez attempted to pass legislation to ease the plight of renters, but was blocked in parliament by opposition parties. Lacking the power to get legislation passed, Sanchez called the early vote in hopes of shoring up more support.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Sanchez's government did end up approving two extraordinary decrees introducing measures similar to the housing reforms rejected by parliament.
"We won't stop until we transform this country's housing model from top to bottom so that houses are for living instead of being at the service of the [landlord] minority," said Alicia del Rio, spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants' Union.
While most of the protests were peaceful, strikers in front of Madrid's Mercamadrid wholesale market said police had used pepper spray on the crowd, prompting at least 13 people to seek medical attention.
Some airlines later reported disruptions to flights in and out of Spain as some airport and airline workers participated in the strike.
The country has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set ​to grow to more than a million by 2028, according to estimates from the central bank.
With fewer and fewer individuals and families able to buy a home, the number of renters in the country has risen sharply. According to Spain's youth council, the average rent is €1,176 ($1,315). This is equivalent to 99% of the average young person's salary.
The general strike came a day after rail workers launched a strike over two major deadly train crashes this year, making decrepit infrastructure another major issue in the upcoming parliamentary elections.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Spain's government supported Wednesday's strike, saying it was staged "in favor of rights" rather than against anyone. Sources close to Sanchez inner circle have gone so far as to say it is "against the opposition."
Alberto Nunez Feijoo, leader of the conservative People’s Party (PP), had a different take, saying if it was indeed "a strike against the opposition," it was "an absurdity the likes of which does not exist in any other European Union country."
Although the UGT labor union — one of the strike organizers — and Sanchez's socialist PSOE party are two separate institutions, they share a historic founder in Pablo Iglesias Posse.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Nicole Ris, reporting for DW in Madrid, followed the strike closely as it unfolded on Wednesday, saying earlier:
Here in Madrid, apparently, lots of people are still showing up for work, and people I know have clearly said they will not go on strike as they don't see much sense in it — although they all suffer under the cost of living crisis and the housing crisis.
There is also debate about this strike being an "election strike" that could benefit the current government.
"I'm not taking part in this. It's nonsense. The government is supporting it because they hope they'll get enough votes on the 29th so they can carry on," a doorman in Madrid told me.
The government supports the strike, claiming it is being held "in favor of rights" rather than against anyone. Sources close to Sanchez's inner circle have gone so far as to say it is "against the opposition," according to the media here.

articles.title_orig: Ring confirms its camera drone won’t have manual controls after crashing on CBS News
articles.title_zh: Ring confirms its camera drone won’t have manual controls after crashing on CBS News
articles.content_orig:
The Ring Drone Cam will entirely rely on AI autopilot to fly around your home.﻿
The Ring Drone Cam will entirely rely on AI autopilot to fly around your home.﻿
When (or if) Ring’s security camera drone flies into our homes in January, you won’t get the option to pilot it yourself. The Ring Drone Cam relies entirely on an “AI Pilot” system to follow pre-programmed routes and navigate autonomously around obstacles, with no manual control option available — and an embarrassing demonstration with CBS News might reveal why.
The video, broadcast on CBS Mornings and published on Threads , shows Ring founder Jamie Siminoff allowing technology reporter Jo Ling Kent to manually fly an early version of the drone via a mobile app with integrated controls.
Ling Kent: “Can I control it?”
Siminoff: “Yeah, so we can load manual controls.”
The demo then shows the drone crashing twice while being manually piloted. In the first instance, Ring reportedly told CBS News that the drone’s collision avoidance technology malfunctioned, and declined to share the video recorded by the drone prior to crashing. CBS News caught the second crash on camera, with the footage showing the drone colliding with a wall after failing to respond to manual controls. According to Siminoff, this occurred because the drone lost internet connectivity — which it also relies on to fly autonomously.
“If it loses connectivity, it’s supposed to stop and land,” Siminoff said in the video. “It did not there.”
Ring declined to show us the app in our own demonstration of the Drone Cam, and said it only works on pre-programmed flight paths. It seems that while manual flight controls were included at some stage of development, Ring won’t be making the feature available to customers when the Drone Cam launches in January.
“We explored a lot of features throughout the development, but autonomous flight to patrol points using the AI Pilot is the best customer benefit and experience,” Ring spokesperson Sam McGee said in a statement to The Verge . Ring didn’t respond to our question regarding whether the decision to not include manual controls was made following the CBS News demo.

articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: US FDA shelves commissioner's voucher program for speedy drug reviews, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
No new drugs have been given a voucher under the FDA 's fast-track review program since Marty Makary left the agency in May. According to internal documents and six sources familiar with the matter, the initiative has now been shelved. The shelving of the National Priority Voucher program has not been previously reported.
The Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program was launched in June 2025, during the Trump administration. Its aim was to compress drug review timelines to as little as one to two months for therapies addressing national priorities, such as urgent unmet health needs. Once presented as a bold fix for U.S. pharmaceutical regulation, the initiative has effectively stalled.
Critics, however, pointed to possible preferential treatment for companies meeting President Donald Trump 's demands, such as offering drugs at lower prices. The program has been left adrift, offering a stark window into the internal chaos, infighting, and lack of steady leadership that has plagued the FDA, which has been without a commissioner since May.
A key component of the scheme, an executive council of political appointees that oversaw drug reviews and had a central role in speeding approvals, has gone dormant, internal documents show. Of the 22 drugs given a voucher, a dozen have been approved, including five since Makary's departure. For several drugs, the program sped approval by eight months or more.
A source familiar with the process said FDA leadership told companies the agency is not moving forward with the program but is keeping applications open. When companies submit them, they don't advance, he said. Rich Danker, a former assistant secretary at the Department of Health and Human Services , said the initiative is quietly being phased out, pointing to the departure of the program's top administrator.
He said no new vouchers have been awarded. HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard said the pilot is ongoing and that the FDA is reviewing feedback from a June public hearing on it to refine the framework. The agency did not respond to requests for comment about the departure of the program's lead or whether it had appointed a new program coordinator.
The pilot had drawn fierce criticism from regulatory experts over the handpicking of drugs and the makeup of the council, which included former acting drug center director Tracy Beth Hoeg and former biologics chief Vinay Prasad.
Both left the FDA earlier this year.
Holly Fernandez Lynch, a health policy professor at the University of Pennsylvania, described the program as “the worst of both worlds,” combining serious risks of political influence with potentially limited practical benefit since many drugs might have qualified for other speedy (review) pathways.
During the June public hearing on the pilot, former FDA executive Peter Lurie criticized the program for ceding review decisions to political appointees, risking consumer safety with compressed timelines, and lacking transparency, echoing other medical experts, patient groups, and industry figures. Critics noted awards granted to companies that reached drug-pricing deals with the White House, such as Eli Lilly LLY.N and Novo Nordisk NOVob.CO.
Germany's Merck KGaA MRCG.DE said in August it received a voucher for its fertility treatment Pergoveris as part of its drug-price agreement with the administration this year. Lilly, Novo and Merck KGaA declined to comment. The review of Sanofi 's SASY.PA diabetes drug Tzield is one example of the council's role in the approval process.
Tasked with evaluating the primary review team's recommendation, Hoeg withheld her approval of the drug. At three separate executive council meetings between October 2025 and April, she repeatedly raised safety objections. After she and Makary left, agency staff quickly granted accelerated approval in June.
Hoeg, a sports medicine physician who opposed COVID-19 vaccines and pandemic policies, told Reuters she is concerned about children being prescribed Tzield, saying a clinical trial showed "minimal at most" benefit when weighed against the product's safety risks. Sanofi said the FDA concluded the drug's benefits outweighed the risks and detailed its scientific rationale in a public memo.
Of the two latest voucher applications for new drugs cleared since Makary left, Merck's MRK.N cholesterol pill Lipfendra and Revolution Medicines' RVMD.O pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque, documents show neither was vetted by the executive council. Rasonque was approved on a swift timeline typical for breakthrough cancer therapies using the agency's preexisting oncology review mechanisms.
Despite a high-profile Oval Office rollout with the company's CEO last year to tout new fertility initiatives, Merck KGaA's supposedly prioritized Pergoveris remains unapproved three months after the FDA accepted its final application following an eight-month rolling review. Merck KGaA and Revolution declined to comment on the review process, while US-based Merck did not respond to a comment request.
For the nine drugs still in the program, FDA career scientists have resumed overseeing review timelines, two sources said.

articles.title_orig: COP31: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'
articles.title_zh: COP31: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'
articles.content_orig:
Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms
Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit.
Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.
She described seeing bright, lush coral beneath the water of her home island in July that had been bleached white just months later.
“It’s time to wake up,” said Heine. “Our response to the threat of overshoot must be overwhelming, or the world we know is over.”
Mia Mottley, the prime minister of Barbados, also called out governments who had “not tried hard enough” to curb emissions since the Paris agreement.
“The UN tells us that, even if every pledge is delivered, we are heading for 2.6 degrees,” she said. “On current policies, 2.8 degrees is where we will end up.
“Let me be plain: overshoot is not a new target. It is a debt, a debt of heat, borrowed against our children’s future. And it must be repaid.”
The opening of the summit of international leaders, on day three of Cop31, saw impassioned speeches interspersed with vigorous displays of Turkish music and dancing.
António Guterres, the UN secretary general, blamed a deceitful fossil fuel industry and countries that “keep expanding fossil fuel production while claiming to be committed to 1.5C”. His speech – a salvo aimed at boosting the talks – was one of the last Guterres, a vocal climate advocate, will deliver as secretary general before he stands down next month.
“We need an extraordinary acceleration,” Guterres said. “Our planet is heating up. The clock is winding down. It’s make or bake time.
“Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs,” he added. “And that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby – fossil fuels do.”
Guterres said oil and gas companies had distorted science and delayed action on the climate crisis, and called for a windfall tax on their bumper profits they have made from the Iran war. “It’s time to kick the habit and end the fossil-fuel addiction,” he said, to applause. “It’s time for governments to tax these windfall profits and use them to help vulnerable countries recover. Polluters must pay.”
Unusually, Turkey is co-hosting Cop with Australia, with the leaders of both countries, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Anthony Albanese respectively, each praising the partnership.
Erdoğan said he wants Cop31 to be remembered as a turning point in the climate crisis and called on countries to act, rather than just make promises. “Every minute we fail to meet the targets in the Paris agreement, the risks and costs we face continue to grow,” the Turkish president said. However, on Monday, away from the conference hall, ​​Erdoğan celebrated the discovery of two new oilfields with an estimated in-situ potential of 135m barrels.
In her speech before world leaders, Heine said every new oil well drilled and every piece of coal extracted was a threat to her country’s future. Without naming any individual oil or gas producer, she added: “The discovery of new fossil fuel resources is not something to celebrate but something to fear.”
Albanese said the conference was a “historic moment” for Australia. The country is one of the world’s biggest exporters of coal and liquified gas. Albanese said governments had a “solemn responsibility” to act on the climate crisis, but he was criticised for failing to mention fossil fuels in his speech.
The gathering of leaders was relatively threadbare. While 91 national leaders attended, according to the UN, major figures such as Donald Trump of the US and Xi Jinping of China were absent. Perhaps tellingly, some other leaders who declined to attend, including the French president, Emmanuel Macron, and the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, are instead heading to Ireland for a conference on AI.
Almost every country at Cop31 is lagging in cutting emissions, with insufficient finance for the nations most vulnerable to extreme heat, floods, fires and other climate-fuelled calamities.
Although the world is barrelling past the 1.5C limit and is entering the teeth of one of the strongest El Niño events in history , there is little sign that the talks will feature any further progress on phasing out planet-heating fossil fuels.
“I’m getting a feeling of panic from around here, from the science community,” said Bill Hare, a climate scientist and chief executive of Climate Analytics, who described fraught conversations with rainforest and cryosphere scientists. “The mood is gradually darkening among scientists. In fact, people talk about feeling as though things have gone backwards.”
Small island nations face an existential threat from rising sea levels and are some of the countries most exposed to catastrophe when global heating shoots past 1.5C. The UN Environment Programme has found that such overshoot is now inevitable, and warned that its effects on icy regions will be so calamitous it should be kept as brief and low as possible.
Other world leaders stressed the urgency of this moment of multiple crises and the need for multilateralism to finally deliver. Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova, the president of North Macedonia, said: “We are the first generation to fully understand the consequences of our choices – and perhaps the last with time to change course. Future generations will live with the consequences of our decisions.”
Nataša Pirc Musar, the president of Slovenia, said: “If we cannot agree that human dignity and respect for nature must be at the heart of our decisions then, frankly, what is left to unite us?”

articles.title_orig: China’s diaspora crackdown reaches deep into Europe, report finds
articles.title_zh: China’s diaspora crackdown reaches deep into Europe, report finds
articles.content_orig:
THE HAGUE — Beijing is overseeing nearly 1,250 overseas policing outposts in more than 90 countries to crack down on dissidents, according to a report by a human rights advocacy organization.
The report described Europe as a hotspot with hundreds of Beijing’s policing offices across some two dozen European countries, which it said exposed China’s growing attempts to control its diaspora.
Researchers at the Spain-based organization, Safeguard Defenders, gathered open-source evidence from the Chinese Party-state to examine the extent to which the Chinese diaspora is monitored, surveilled and policed around the world.
These policing outposts “act as the Chinese Communist Party operatives for community surveillance and enforcement abroad,” according to the report.
The report lands at an awkward time for Europe’s trade officials. Ditte Juul Jørgensen, head of the EU’s trade department — which has been working to balance the trade relationship with Beijing — will meet with China’s Vice Minister of Commerce Ling Ji in Brussels on Thursday.
Europe is attempting to walk a fine line with its relations with Beijing. EU legislation proposed in January seeks to kick risky Chinese suppliers out of Europe’s most critical industries over cybersecurity concerns, while supply chain dependencies and political coercion remain ongoing challenges. The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas has also raised concerns about what she said was China’s enabling of Russia’s war in Ukraine and credible reports of China training Russia’s military .
The report builds on initial revelations from Safeguard Defenders in 2022 that identified more than 100 facilities around the world, which the NGO described as overseas outposts of China’s security apparatus. Back then, that report said Beijing announced its “first batch” of “30 overseas police service stations in 25 cities in 21 countries.”
Following the revelations, some governments denounced the overseas police stations as illegal, and some pursued criminal investigations, the NGO said in its latest report. In response, Beijing claimed the stations had been closed, it added.
“Far from closing, the evidence shows expansion: today more than 10 police forces from five Chinese provinces work through a global network of Chinese Communist Party operatives abroad,” the new report says.
The latest paper was presented at a conference hosted by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), a gathering of 52 cross-party lawmakers from 30 countries that campaigns for a more coordinated response to the Chinese Communist Party. Policymakers raised numerous concerns at the event in The Hague earlier this month — about what they considered security threats of critical infrastructure, trade dependencies and potential risks from a future conflict between China and Taiwan that would disrupt shipping.
The Chinese foreign ministry and state media have previously called IPAC an “anti-China” group and accused it of spreading disinformation and interfering in China’s internal affairs, particularly over Taiwan.
China’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs and its European Union mission didn’t respond to requests for comment on the report. China has previously denied running overseas police stations and says it doesn’t interfere in other countries’ internal affairs and that it respects international law.
In 2023, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson rejected the term “police stations,” saying the “institutions helped overseas Chinese who could not return to China due to the pandemic, renew their driving licence and perform physical examination.”
These 1,250 offices were “the tip of the iceberg,” according to the NGO, which said it was conservative in how it mapped and linked them to China’s policing system. To be counted, they had to be officially connected to China’s police or prosecutors and have open-source evidence of overseas activities, report author Laura Harth said. This meant broader influence or interference operations were excluded.
“All of them serve to control and instill fear in diaspora communities … all of them represent a standing national security risk,” she said.
Slovakian MEP Miriam Lexmann, who is part of the European Parliament’s trade committee and China delegation — lawmakers tasked with maintaining and managing legislative ties between the EU and China — said people needed to become more aware of the security threats posed by China.
“It means that our free countries are no longer free anymore for everyone because they are not able to guarantee freedom of speech, freedom of behavior to people who are in our country,” she told POLITICO in reference to the operations.
China’s surveillance through facial recognition and interference in communications was “the exact behavior of the former Soviet Stasi,” she said, but worse since the technology is now much more sophisticated.
The main concern expressed by lawmakers attending the IPAC conference was China’s relationship with Russia, and its help in propping up the Kremlin’s war in Ukraine. Their discussions included what this could mean for a future conflict and war on two fronts if Beijing were to try and take Taiwan militarily while NATO countries were attacked by Russia.
“The road to escalation in the Taiwan Strait can run right through what’s happening in Ukraine and in Kyiv,” said Dutch lawmaker Jan Paternotte, who co-chaired the IPAC conference.

articles.title_orig: Iran Update, November 11, 2026
articles.title_zh: Iran Update, November 11, 2026
articles.source: Institute for the Study of War
articles.content_orig:
The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) and The Critical Threats Project (CTP) at the American Enterprise Institute are publishing updates Monday through Friday to provide analysis on the war with Iran and the broader Middle East. Weekday updates cover events from the past 24-hour period, whereas weekend updates are abbreviated and cover the Houthi-Saudi conflict and major breaking developments related to the war with Iran.
The US Department of Justice indicted three members of an Iranian-supported Kataib Hezbollah front group on November 10 for their involvement in nearly 20 attacks or plots in Europe and the United States, including an attempted attack on the Royal Air Force (RAF) base in Fairford in September 2026.[1] The three individuals conducted numerous attacks in Europe between March and May 2026 as part of the group known as Harakat Ashab al Yamin al Islamiya.[2] The Justice Department described Harakat Ashab al Yamin al Islamiya as a front group for Kataib Hezbollah and the IRGC.[3] Both Iran and the Iraqi militias have historically used front groups to provide plausible deniability and obfuscate their involvement in attacks and other activity.[4] The Justice Department indicted senior Kataib Hezbollah commander Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawoud al Saadi in May 2026 for his direction of Harakat Ashab al Yamin al Islamiya‘s attacks.[5] Saadi more recently organized the plot targeting RAF Fairford from prison in New York.[6] UK authorities thwarted a plot to attack US bombers stationed at the base with small explosive drones on September 27, which led the United States to relocate the bombers from the base.[7]
The front group’s pattern of activity suggests that its operations are part of an Iranian effort to compel Israel and the United States to halt attacks on Iran. The front group targeted and attempted to target numerous Jewish sites in Europe and the United States in March and April 2026, including synagogues.[8] The attacks likely aimed to retaliate against US-Israeli strikes in Iran by spreading terror and fear among US and European Jewish communities, thereby increasing the pressure on both countries to end the strike campaign. Such a strategy may reflect Iran’s recognition that previous direct Iranian attacks on Israeli soil failed to compel Israeli decisionmakers to avoid taking action against Iran.[9]
Limited US strikes on Iran in August and September, as well as reports that the United States was considering renewed strikes on Iran, may have motivated the cell’s shift from Jewish-affiliated targets to US military targets.[10]  The group paused attacks on any targets after Saadi was sentenced in the United States in May 2026. The Justice Department noted that the three men began to plan the RAF Fairford attack in August.[11] UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the House of Commons in mid-October that the IRGC ”almost certainly” directed the plot.[12] Attacks on US bases that support US operations, such as RAF Fairford, are likely intended to deter future US attacks on Iran. Iranian officials have increasingly issued threats against US bases in Europe amid expectations that the United States could imminently strike Iran again. Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned Arabic-language media on November 11 that Iran would target distant US bases in the event of any new attack, for example.[13] It is not clear if Rezaei is threatening to conduct direct missile or drone attacks against such bases or referring to sabotage. Several US bases in Europe lie within the range of Iran’s existing missiles.[14] The Wall Street Journal reported on November 10 that US forces relocated multiple tankers from the RAF Mildenhall Base to Germany and other countries due to an imminent threat from Iran, citing people familiar with the matter.[15]
Ansar al Furqan, a Baloch Salafi-jihadi group, has at least partially merged into the Mobarizoun Popular Front (MPF), a coalition of Baloch anti-regime groups that has conducted several operations in Sistan and Baluchistan Province in recent months.[16] The MPF claimed that the merger would unite Baloch armed groups and increase the effectiveness of anti-regime operations. [17] Jaish al Adl and several other Baloch militant groups formed the MPF in December 2025 to fight against the regime and increase coordination among anti-regime groups in southeastern Iran.[18] Ansar al Furqan did not publicly join the MPF when the coalition formed and continued to operate independently. MPF Spokesperson Mahmoud Baloch announced on November 11 that Ansar al Furqan had merged into the MPF after unspecified Baloch figures mediated between the groups.[19]  It is unclear at this time how fully Ansar al Furqan has merged into the MPF. An anti-regime Baloch media outlet subsequently reported that Ansar al Furqan spokesperson Molavi Nasrollah Baloch confirmed the full merger.[20] An alleged direct statement from Ansar al Furqan alternatively suggested that only a small number of its fighters chose to join the MPF on their own initiative and that Ansar al Furqan’s foundational structure and principal divisions remain intact.[21] The discrepancies in reporting about Ansar al Furqan‘s decision to join the MPF may reflect internal splits within the group, although available reporting does not identify the defectors or explain why they joined the MPF. This merger comes amid an uptick in anti-regime militant activity in southeastern Iran in recent months.[22]
Ansar al Furqan and the MPF share the common objective to overthrow the Iranian regime, which may explain in part Ansar al Furqan’s decision to join the MPF at this time. Ansar al Furqan called the MPF fighters its “brothers” and expressed support for their anti-regime struggle, which indicates that the groups share a common enemy despite their ideological differences.[23] The MPF’s charter identifies “deep political change” in Iran as its central objective and frames its struggle around the regime’s oppression of Baloch citizens and other Iranians.[24] The MPF has explicitly called for the overthrow of the Velayat-e Faqih [the Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist] system, but the coalition has not advocated for Baloch independence or autonomy.[25] The MPF contains Salafi-jihadi groups, such as Jaish al Adl, but the coalition itself has not expressed Salafi-jihadi views.  Ansar al Furqan also seeks the regime’s collapse but frames its campaign as jihad and emphasizes the role of religious scholars in its leadership.[26] Ansar al Furqan has used sectarian terms to refer to the Iranian regime and Shia groups, whereas the MPF promotes cooperation among Iranians across ideological divisions.[27]  Shared objectives to collapse the regime may have encouraged some fighters to join the MPF, while strict ideological adherence may have compelled other Ansar al Furqan fighters to remain independent. Ideological differences between Ansar al Furqan and the MPF could lead to disagreements over rhetoric, recruitment, or ideology that could limit the feasibility of the partnership.
The Ansar al Furqan fighters who joined the MPF may increase the coalition’s capabilities through additional manpower and combat experience. It is unclear how many Ansar al Furqan fighters have joined the MPF, however. Ansar al Furqan has conducted some tactically sophisticated attacks, including a large-scale attack against a Law Enforcement Command (LEC) checkpoint in Fahraj, Kerman Province, in December 2025.[28] The MPF has already demonstrated the ability to conduct complex operations across southeastern Iran, including a nine-hour engagement in Saravan in September and a combined improvised explosive device (IED) and small-arms attack in Jalgh in October.[29]  The impacts of Ansar al Furqan’s merger on the MPF’s capabilities will also depend on the extent to which the MPF incorporates these fighters into the MPF’s command structures.
Nothing significant to report.
Assessed Iranian War Aims:
Nothing

Shares of AMD and Broadcom rose in response, with the two being viewed as potential beneficiaries of a prolonged governance crisis at what is arguably their biggest rival.
The allegations: Huang admitted an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data-center company that is a large Nvidia customer. US intelligence reportedly suspects her of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Read more (Nov 10, 2026)
The probes: The board has opened an investigation, and Trump said the FBI is looking into it. Nvidia says it has "no reason to believe" secrets were compromised.
The damage: Over two sessions, about $427B of market value was erased. Baird downgraded the stock to neutral. Morgan Stanley dropped it from its Top Pick list, and BofA removed it from its U.S. 1 List. Read more (Nov 11, 2026)

Prices are the Nov 11 close. Fair value and analyst targets are as of Nov 11–12, 2026.
These are computed as the Nov 11 close divided by next-fiscal-year consensus EPS:
Nvidia is cheap on paper, and that is the tension. Revenue grew 65.5% last fiscal year to $215.94B, with a 71.1% gross margin. Next quarter's consensus is $108.8B in revenue and $2.47 EPS, ahead of the Nov 17 report. It beat on both lines in its last two quarters. Estimates were not cut, with EPS revisions at +5.2% over 90 days. The discount reflects governance and China risk, not weaker fundamentals. Wells Fargo still expects a revenue beat. The risk is that a CEO exit or new China export controls hit a stock already down 23% in a month.
AMD is the momentum story. Its Q3 beat on Nov 3 was EPS $2.09 vs $1.94, and the stock rose 4.7%. EPS estimates have been revised up about 10% in 30 days. Consensus has revenue rising from $52.1B (FY2026) to $95.7B (FY2027). The stock is up 152.6% YTD but still about 16% below its $658.52 high. The fair-value model sits below the price, so much of the growth is already priced in.
Broadcom is the laggard that is catching up. It is about 30% below its $495 high and down 17% over three months. Its last two prints beat estimates, yet the stock fell 13% and 3.4% afterward, which shows how high the bar is. Estimates are flat over 90 days (-0.9%). The supports are JPMorgan's view of its Google TPU role and Anthropic's compute commitment. Read more (Nov 10, 2026) Its next report is Dec 9 .
The rise in AMD and Broadcom is a rotation, not a new thesis. Hyperscaler budgets set AI spending, not Nvidia's headlines. Both stocks also rallied with the whole chip sector after a steep selloff.
Case for: Broadcom has the best setup on valuation. It trades at about 18x next-year EPS, its fair-value model shows upside, and a pullback came before this bounce. AMD has the strongest estimate momentum.
Case against: Neither stock has structurally gained from Nvidia's trouble. BofA says share gains depend on prolonged scrutiny. A quick resolution, or a strong Nov 17 report, could send money back to Nvidia. Rate risk is also growing after a hot CPI print. Read more (Nov 9, 2026)
Levels: NVIDIA (NVDA) falling below its 52-week low of $164.27 would mark a new phase of the sell-off. Broadcom (AVGO) reclaiming $350 would extend its rebound.
The data favors Broadcom's valuation setup over AMD's. Nvidia is the highest-variance case. It has the cheapest multiple and the biggest governance overhang, and there is no way to price the board's decision.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week that illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, two people familiar with the matter told CNN.
Trump officials have long harbored concerns that Megaspeed has circumvented US law and funneled advanced chips into China — a prospect that Treasury staffers argued should land it on Commerce’s so-called entity list of China-connected companies that could pose national security risks. But the issue gathered newfound attention and importance in recent days when Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Megaspeed employee suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Senior Trump officials, including Lutnick, also were briefed months ago about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who the intelligence community suspected of being a Chinese spy, people familiar with the matter said.
But despite those warnings, Commerce has so far refused to put Megaspeed on the entity list, the people said.
Confronted on it by Bessent last Thursday, Lutnick did not immediately commit to taking any specific action, they said.
Axios first reported the Situation Room confrontation.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company that was originally incorporated in 2015 as a Chinese video game developer called 7Road International. But in the three years since Alice Huang became director and the company changed its name, it has become one of the largest buyers of Nvidia chips in Asia , purchasing more than $4 billion worth of its semiconductors, by some analyst estimates.
Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing and said it is a “compliant and legal company.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”
The entity list represents one of the US’s most significant tools for preventing American firms from selling their products to foreign companies and organizations. But adding Megaspeed to the list could also risk inflaming tensions with China amid Trump’s efforts to manage the US’ trade relationship with the fellow superpower. The Commerce Department hasn’t added any company to the list in more than a year.
Representatives for the Treasury and Commerce departments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.title_zh: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.content_orig:
A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2 , can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618 , it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday.
Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
An attacker who can reach the server needs no authentication to exploit the flaw and could take full control of the server process, the Linux vendor says. It rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported.
HTTP/2 runs only where the Protocols directive turns it on, as the module documentation explains. The directive uses h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS and h2c for HTTP/2 over plain TCP. It can be set for the whole server or for a single virtual host, so admins should check the server-wide setting and every virtual host.
Standalone builds of the module, released on GitHub as mod_h2, are affected from version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Admins who run the Apache HTTP Server project's own releases should move to version 2.4.71, the fixed release named in its security advisory . That release also fixes a crash in mod_md, rated important, and a one-byte overwrite of stack memory in mod_vhost_alias, rated low.
The distributions in the table below ship their own builds of the server, with their own package version numbers. On Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, for example, the fix ships as mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1.
Red Hat shipped fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 yesterday and rates the flaw Important on those releases rather than Critical. Their mod_http2 packages give each HTTP/2 stream its own memory allocator, which makes an attack much harder, according to the vendor's severity assessment . Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier do not contain the vulnerable code.
The Debian rows come from Debian's security tracker , and the Amazon row from the Amazon Linux tracker . Ubuntu's CVE tracker had no page for the flaw when The Hacker News checked it today.
The Apache HTTP Server advisory offers no workaround. In its vulnerability analysis , Wiz advises admins who cannot update yet to remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive, leaving Protocols http/1.1.
The standalone mod_h2 project has published no fixed release so far. Its release list on GitHub ends at 2.0.42, the last affected version, and its repository has been read-only since it was archived on June 9. The Protocols change above also applies to servers that use those builds.
The flaw was reported on October 26 by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, a free scanning service for open-source projects that uses the company's AI models. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research reported it last week.
An earlier HTTP/2 flaw , CVE-2026-23918, was fixed in version 2.4.67, released on May 4. Servers updated to that release, or to any later one up to 2.4.70, still run a version that the new flaw affects.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Tumbles as Investors Consider Future Without CEO Huang
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Tumbles as Investors Consider Future Without CEO Huang
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang soon, according to two sources familiar with the matter, following allegations that Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.
The Trump administration is aware of the matter, the sources said.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on the board's moves.
Nvidia's share price slid more than 8% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the Journal's report, extending a multi-day sell-off for one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies.
The company has faced days of turmoil following reports that American intelligence agencies believed Huang was the target of a Chinese spying plot.
Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993, and for years it was best known for designing graphics cards widely used for gaming. The company now designs the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.
The New York Times reported last week on allegations that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who previously led a Singapore-based firm called Megaspeed International that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and hardware. U.S. intelligence agencies have believed for months that Alice Huang — who is not related to Jensen Huang — was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the newspaper reported.
In a message to Nvidia employees over the weekend, Jensen Huang wrote that he was "unfaithful to my wife" and apologized for hurting her and their children. He did not name the woman involved.
Nvidia's board said Sunday it had launched an independent investigation into allegations that the CEO "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said, "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the U.S. government would have notified us."
Two law enforcement sources told CBS News the Justice Department is also investigating Megaspeed over potential violations of U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI chips. Some analysts have raised questions about whether the saga resulted in China — which is racing the U.S. for AI dominance — gaining access to Nvidia's technology through Megaspeed. The company has denied any involvement in illegal chip transfers.
China has denied all allegations, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun telling reporters on Monday that the "so-called Chinese spy narrative is entirely baseless and constitutes slander and smear."
Beyond the national security concerns, Nvidia is facing a securities lawsuit accusing the company of failing to disclose information to shareholders about Jensen Huang's relationship with the alleged spy.
Jensen Huang has a close relationship with the Trump administration. President Trump gave Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 computer chips to "approved customers" in China late last year, with the federal government taking a 25% cut of chip sales. The deal did not include Nvidia's more advanced Blackwell or Rubin systems.
The Nvidia CEO and other U.S. tech executives traveled to China with Mr. Trump earlier this year.
On Monday, Mr. Trump called Jensen Huang a "very high-quality person," saying during a White House briefing that "the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape." The president said he spoke to Jensen Huang to see how he was doing, and the executive "said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."

articles.title_zh: Senior US Democratic senators urge administration to preserve Nvidia export records amid China security concerns
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
WASHINGTON — The Trump administration has briefed top lawmakers on a growing national security crisis around the world’s leading chipmaker, Nvidia, after its chief executive, Jensen Huang, admitted over the weekend to an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy .
Senior U.S. intelligence officials briefed the Gang of Eight — congressional leaders from both parties, and the chairs and vice chairs of the House and Senate intelligence committees — on the matter, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday.
Congressional Republicans have called on Huang himself to provide an update, warning the incident raised “significant national security concerns” that could have compromised cutting-edge American technology at a critical moment in the race with China for supremacy in artificial intelligence.
Huang admitted Sunday to having an affair with Alice Huang, who was identified as a Chinese intelligence asset by U.S. authorities, after the New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had raised concerns within the administration about his potential compromise.
Nvidia’s board of directors said Sunday it will launch an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang, after he revealed he had an affair with a former Chinese executive.
President Trump is scheduled to visit China next week.
“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Jensen Huang said in a statement Sunday.
“Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports,” he added, “NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.”
Debate over export controls for the world’s most advanced semiconductor chips, produced by Nvidia, has raged over the last eight years in Washington, with lawmakers across party lines expressing concern that Chinese access to the chips could strengthen their hand in the development of the most powerful AI models.
Huang has been one of the most vocal opponents of the U.S. export controls, calling them a “mistake” and saying they were hurting American businesses more than they were constricting Chinese government efforts.
The executive was successful in lobbying the Trump administration to ease export restrictions on some of Nvidia’s most advanced chips over the past year.
Jeffries said he would be calling for greater export controls on chips after the incident. The New York congressman is expected to become the next speaker of the House after Democrats swept into power in this month’s midterm elections.
“We’re going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue,” Jeffries said, adding that “real concerns” have arisen from the case that will need to be addressed.
U.S. intelligence unmasked the Chinese intelligence operation after intercepting the communications of Alice Huang, a former journalist with Chinese state media who later became a senior executive at Megaspeed International. The Singaporean data center firm was already under the microscope for allegedly funneling restricted AI chips to Beijing.
Trump was reportedly made aware of the Chinese espionage effort targeting Huang, but chose not to act, according to the New York Times.
Nvidia’s stock dropped more than 4% Monday , after the board said it would open an investigation into its chief executive  being the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
The company “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” it said in the statement.
Some of the world’s leading financiers are sounding increasingly alarmed about an AI bubble.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it continued. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Rubio declined to address questions from reporters on the matter Monday.
“It’s an internal corporate matter for them, so I’m just not going to comment on that topic,” the secretary of State and national security advisor said.
But the administration could face increased calls to investigate Jensen Huang, a Trump ally, who traveled with Trump to Beijing in May and attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping in September held at the White House.
Republicans have also formally requested Huang appear before the House on Nov. 18 — when Trump will be in China — to brief them on what happened.
Rep. Brian Mast of Florida, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Rick Crawford of Arkansas, head of the House Intelligence Committee, and Rep. John Moolenaar of Michigan, who leads the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, said the issue of Chinese infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology “is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.”
“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk,” they wrote.

articles.title_orig: The world's super-rich are piling into alternative investments. Here's why
articles.title_zh: The world's super-rich are piling into alternative investments. Here's why
articles.content_orig:
The world's wealthiest investors are increasingly looking beyond stocks and bonds, pouring money into hedge funds, private equity and infrastructure assets, as market volatility and fears about stubborn inflation spur diversification.
From Asian billionaires to global family offices, alternative investments are becoming a bigger part of portfolios once dominated by traditional assets, said industry watchers
JPMorgan Asset Management's private wealth alternative assets in Asia-Pacific surged 40% over the past 12 months, according to Dan Watkins, the firm's regional chief executive officer, underscoring the growing appetite among high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
"So you really have this huge appetite for alternative exposure happening in that ultra-high-net-worth, high-net-worth category," Watkins said recently at a media summit in Singapore.
The shift comes as investors grapple with increasingly concentrated equity markets, geopolitical uncertainty and concerns that stocks and bonds may not provide the same protection against market downturns as they once did, experts said.
"We are seeing a sharp increase in planned asset allocation to alternatives among the family offices we speak to," said John Woods, chief investment officer for Asia at Lombard Odier.
Alternative investments now account for 60% of single-family office portfolios, surpassing traditional assets for the first time, according to BNY Wealth . Traditional assets accounted for 41% of allocations, the report found.
Wealthy investors are seeking diversification, income and access to investments outside listed markets, and concerns over elevated valuations, tight credit spreads and the growing correlation between stocks and bonds have accelerated the trend, Woods added.
Hedge funds are emerging as a favored option among wealthy investors seeking protection against market swings, particularly as traditional diversification strategies face growing challenges.
Olaolu Aganga, head of portfolio construction and analytics at Citi Wealth, said hedge funds have attracted the strongest recent interest among qualified clients, who are seeking returns less dependent on the direction of equity markets.
Private credit is another area drawing interest, offering investors contractual income streams, while some hedge fund strategies seek to profit from differences in performance between companies rather than relying on broad market rallies, said Woods.
Citi's 2026 survey of 351 family offices found that inflation was their biggest concern, followed by interest rates, financial system stability and market volatility.
Wealthy families are increasingly seeking investments that can generate income and help preserve purchasing power amid persistent inflation and interest-rate uncertainty, while diversifying portfolios against market volatility, according to Aganga.
The Citi survey, however, also showed public equities recorded the strongest net increase in allocations, suggesting wealthy investors are adding alternatives rather than abandoning traditional markets. "This is not a wholesale rotation away from public markets," Woods said.
Infrastructure has emerged as another major beneficiary of the shift, with the artificial intelligence boom creating enormous demand for data centers, electricity networks and digital connectivity.
Thomas Roland Guyot, head of private markets investment specialists for Southeast Asia at UBS Unified Global Alternatives, said investors are increasingly targeting assets that support AI, electrification and energy security.
Such investments potentially offer a combination of long-term growth and relatively predictable cash flows, particularly where revenues are supported by essential demand or long-term contracts.
Investor appetite is already showing up in fund flows. Net inflows into open-ended infrastructure funds rose 30% year on year in the 12 months through the first quarter of 2026, according to PitchBook data cited by UBS.
Private equity remains a cornerstone of wealthy investors' alternative portfolios, although they are becoming more selective. Family offices are increasingly favoring direct investments in companies, co-investments alongside private equity managers and purchases of existing fund stakes on the secondary market, rather than relying solely on traditional pooled funds, according to Citi Wealth's Aganga.
Such approaches can give investors greater control over their investments or opportunities to acquire assets at discounts, said Lombard Odier's Woods.
The broader shift is also being facilitated by the growth of evergreen and semi-liquid funds, which have lowered minimum investment thresholds and reduced some administrative hurdles associated with traditional private-market funds, Woods added.
Investing into alternative assets does not come without risks, even as mitigating those is driving flows.
Private investments can lock up capital for years, while valuations may be slow to reflect deteriorating market conditions. Even funds marketed as semi-liquid can restrict withdrawals when redemption requests surge.
"Improved access does not equal liquidity," JPMorgan's Watkins said.
Citi's Aganga also warned that performance can vary significantly between managers, while private assets may appear less volatile than they actually are because valuations are updated less frequently.
Investors must also guard against unintended concentration. A portfolio holding data centers through real estate, infrastructure and private equity funds may appear diversified while remaining heavily exposed to the same AI investment cycle, UBS' Guyot said.
For now, the flow of capital into alternative assets shows their increasing appeal among the rich, though not at the expense of traditional investment, with Woods pointing out that much of the new investment is being funded by fresh capital and excess cash rather than large-scale sales of stocks and bonds.
